_comment: School Kit — shared strict-TypeScript overlay for Expo apps.
This file deliberately does NOT extend expo/tsconfig.base, even though
an Expo tsconfig must. Reason: `extends` resolves relative to the file
that declares it, `expo` is not a dependency of @school-kit/config, and
pnpm's strict node_modules means it is not hoisted to the repo root
either — so extending it from here fails to resolve. Between Phase 0 and
2026-08-15 this file did carry that extends, which made it unusable by
any consumer; nothing imported it, so the breakage stayed invisible.
Consumers extend BOTH, in this order (TS 5.0+ accepts an array, later
entries win):
"extends": ["expo/tsconfig.base", "@school-kit/config/tsconfig.expo.json"]
expo/tsconfig.base resolves from the app's own node_modules, where expo
genuinely is a dependency; this overlay then applies the project's strict
options on top.
noUncheckedIndexedAccess is the one option here that is not simply
`strict`. It matters more on mobile than on the server: list rendering
and route params are index/lookup-heavy, and an undefined slipping
through renders as a crash in a native view rather than a 500 someone
sees in Sentry.
This overlay deliberately does NOT set `module`. On Expo SDK 52 it had
to: that SDK's base set `target: ESNext` but no `module`, so TypeScript
defaulted to ES2015 and rejected `import.meta` with TS1343. SDK 57's base
sets `module: preserve` + `moduleResolution: bundler` itself, which
supports import.meta natively — verified 2026-08-15 by removing the
override and re-running typecheck clean. Overriding it now would only
downgrade the framework's own, better choice. If a future Expo app pins
an SDK older than 53, it needs `module: esnext` locally rather than a
reinstated override here.
